unavailable_metadata.scope: Public gated-card GET failed; no authentication or weight request attempted.

measurement_roles.fact: Released PEFT sequence-classification adapter is explicitly identified by its card as the CrPO paper quality evaluator. Adapter task_type SEQ_CLS, LoRA rank32, target_modules q_proj/v_proj, modules_to_save classifier/score. Base-only generation is not the trained score function.

Pinned metric/config source uses jinaai/jina-embeddings-v3, cosine distance, lowercase/punctuation removal, unique words, no lemmatization or stopword removal by default; novelty/reference sets and diversity require multiple compatible texts and declared grouping.
Reference-model perplexity is a model/tokenizer-specific measurement; it is not an instruction-prompted creativity judgment or Bayesian surprise. Paper names instruction-tuned Gemma-2-27B.

measurement_roles.role: Training quality injection / evaluator CLI default
measurement_roles.fact: Skywork-Reward-Gemma-2-27B-v0.2 is the external quality signal described for training; evaluate_lm_by_rm CLI also defaults to it. Selecting that default is not selecting the paper MuCE-trained reward evaluator.

paper_code_default_differences.finding: Paper evaluation uses the trained Gemma-2-9B MuCE reward model. CLI defaults to Skywork27B; authors shell examples explicitly pass a local cpo-rm-gemma-2-9b-it-lora-msd5-mm10-ms20 path. Public adapter replaces that inaccessible local path by declared identity; no equivalence is inferred from the default.

Paper describes response surprisal conditional on the prompt. Pinned evaluation source constructs the whole prompt/response conversation and compute_perplexity uses every attention-unmasked shifted token as a label, with no assistant-only loss mask. Code-faithful whole-conversation perplexity must not be silently described as an exact implementation of response-only conditional surprisal.
paper_code_default_differences.status: Static source observation; not executed or empirically quantified.

paper_code_default_differences.finding: Paper novelty equation gives absolute DSI difference; pinned compute_novelty multiplies the absolute difference by2. A later reproduction must declare code-faithful versus formula-faithful choices.
paper_code_default_differences.status: Static source observation; not executed or corrected.

paper_code_default_differences.finding: Upstream groups by task and FullPrompt and optionally checks rating-label equality. Minimum20 and margin5 are inclusive; maximum10 limits accepted pair appearances per response index in greedy input order, not10pairs total per prompt. Stricter source-context grouping and uncapped compatible counts are a comparative eligibility policy, not a byte-identical reconstruction of MuCE-Pref.

training_overlap.scope: Membership overlap between each cached original MuCE train response/prompt group and the exact released quality-adapter training members.

proven_facts.fact: Released adapter card names MuCE as its fine-tuning dataset. Paper describes reward-model training on MuCE preference data.
Adapter config base revision is null and card does not identify a frozen dataset revision, per-response/per-prompt training-membership manifest or training exclusion list.

MuCE-Pref metadata/card identifies a train split of42058 examples and separate val/test/heldout_item/heldout_task splits; no row contents or row inventories were fetched. Public split names and counts do not by themselves identify the adapter training members.

Original MuCE raw preparation maps Set values Training/Validation/Test/HeldoutItem/HeldoutTask/HeldoutLanguage into named splits. This metadata path does not prove independent prompt separation for ordinary response splits.

Source prepare_crpo_data has optional rm_split handling. It does not bind the published adapter to an executed membership manifest; current CLI defaults rm_split0.0, distinct from the Python function default0.8.

Choose development versus validation role and establish training-membership exclusion before interpreting a reward-model result as fresh held-out calibration.

Calibrate any substitution as a new measurement variant; a newer/bigger base or instruction model cannot reproduce learned reward weights, embedding geometry or reference surprisal solely through model-card similarity.
